description: Issue and manage two kinds of credential: inference tokens for calling deployed models, and platform API tokens for the management API and MCP

secret.title: Save this API token now
secret.warning: This API token is shown only once. It cannot be viewed again after this dialog is closed.

title: API Tokens
usageBatches: The same API key also calls the OpenAI-compatible batch API, /v1/files and /v1/batches; examples are on

gateway.title: Inference tokens
gateway.description: For applications calling deployed models (/v1, OpenAI-compatible); they start with gw-. They cannot call the platform management API.

platform.title: Platform API tokens
platform.description: Call the platform management API without signing in, and connect to the MCP service; they start with gwp_. A token acts as you, with your current permissions, narrowed by its scope: a read token can only read; a read-write token can do what you can in the console. Tokens are created and revoked from a signed-in session only.
platform.scopeHelp: MCP needs read only. A read-write token can change the platform; give one only to programs that need it.
platform.revokeConfirm: Revoke “{{name}}”? Programs using it lose access at once.
platform.nameTooLong: Name must not exceed 128 UTF-8 bytes (Chinese characters usually use 3 bytes each)

revoke.confirm: Revoke “{{name}}”? Programs using it lose access at once; its past usage stays in Usage analytics. If no active tokens remain, the gateway refuses every /v1 request until another token is created, unless an administrator turned on keyless access under Settings > Security.

tokens.open: {{tokens}} tokens of {{name}}, open in Usage analytics

scope.label: Model services it can call
scope.required: Choose at least one model service
scope.noneLeftHelp: Every chosen model service has been deleted, so this token cannot call any model now.
scope.editHelp: The token's next request uses the new scope.
